analysis: Both changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md head lines 335-365; docs/architecture/inference.md patch hunk adding 'Model startup calibration' and code-map rows). No source, wire, key, attestation or authorization code changed in this batch. The docs describe provider-local calibration: a one-token startup health check marked EngineMeasurementPurpose.startupWarmup, an excluded 128-token warmup plus two uncached solo probes (<=512 prompt / 32 output tokens), a single process-wide session, a foreground lease (IdleCalibrationCoordinator.beginForeground) that cancels calibration for customer requests, and retirement via EngineV2.submitWithRetirement. The docs state that calibration uses existing KV/service budgets, does not lower activation/OS reserves or raise concurrency, produces no served-request or token counters, and leaves capacity wire fields and the platform memory contract unchanged. Relevant threats are T-010 (cancellation/GPU consumption), T-029 (idle GPU), T-007 and T-041. Calibration probes are synthetic and local; the docs do not claim prefix-cache or cacheSalt behavior, so no T-041 or SEC-035 change is evident, though the docs do not say whether probes bypass SSD donation and TTFT-oracle surfaces. A later pass that sees the Swift sources should check: (1) probes never donate to or read the SSD prefix cache; (2) the foreground lease really cancels and waits for retirement without delaying customer deadlines; (3) capacity evidence published through heartbeats is not an unauthenticated trust input to coordinator routing or billing (T-007 class); (4) calibration probe prompts and outputs are not logged. None of these can be assessed from this documentation-only diff, so no finding is raised.
